# Summary: 2010 Election Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a vision for Britain's future, addressing economic challenges, public services, social policy, and political reform following the 2008 financial crisis and parliamentary expenses scandal.

## Economic Recovery and Growth
The document prioritises securing economic recovery through continued government spending support while committing to halving the deficit within four years via growth, fair taxation, and spending cuts. Key proposals include banking reform, creating a £4 billion fund for growing businesses, developing high-tech industries, investing in infrastructure (including high-speed rail and broadband), and supporting one million skilled jobs by 2015.

## Employment and Welfare
The manifesto emphasises welfare reform requiring work capability for benefit recipients, guaranteeing jobs for long-term unemployed, and ensuring work pays better than benefits. The National Minimum Wage would rise with average earnings, while a £40 weekly "Better Off in Work" guarantee would support employment.

## Public Services
**Education** spending would increase for frontline services, with expanded nursery provision, guaranteed catch-up tuition, and 75% of young people entering higher education or advanced training by age 30.

**Healthcare** reforms include legally binding patient guarantees covering waiting times, cancer testing, and GP access, alongside preventative care expansion and more home-based treatment options.

## Social Policy
Family support includes flexible parental leave and a new Toddler Tax Credit. For pensioners, the manifesto promises earnings-linked state pensions and a new National Care Service providing free home care for those with greatest needs, with residential care costs capped after two years.

## Crime and Immigration
Proposals include maintaining police numbers, faster anti-social behaviour responses, and an Australian-style points-based immigration system requiring newcomers to earn citizenship.

## Political Reform
Democratic renewal proposals include referendums on electoral reform, fixed-term parliaments, an elected second chamber, stronger lobbying regulations, and exploring lowering voting age to 16.

## Environment and International
Environmental commitments target 40% low-carbon electricity by 2020, while international priorities include completing operations abroad, EU engagement, and meeting overseas aid commitments.
